item.title: Log10x App - v1.3.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\- An add-on's data models and \`tstats\` can read compact events: one \`props.conf\` line indexes each event under its original sourcetype, with the fields its Receiver attaches. This needs the Receiver at release 1.1.183 or later. \- \`tx\` and \`txf\` also return the raw events of the same sources, such as those indexed before the Receiver, that the new \`tenx-raw-events\` macro names. \- Events the Receiver sends as their own text, in the same stream as compact events, come back as they are through \`tx\`, \`txf\`, the dashboards and compiled alerts. \- A Universal Forwarder can read compact events from files that carry the fields the Receiver attaches and each event's time. \- A \`tx\` word search keeps its answer for each word, so a later search for the same word reads only the templates stored since. \- In a search that transforms its events, \`txf\` applies only the rules that produce the fields the search reads, at the top level and inside \`union\`. \- Compact events index the Receiver's pattern hash \`tenx_pattern\`, pattern name \`message_pattern\` and level \`severity_level\` when their record holds them, so \`| tstats count where index\=\ by tenx_pattern\` counts by pattern without expansion. \- The README shows how Fluent Bit sends the Receiver's events to the HTTP Event Collector with their attached fields as indexed fields, which the data models of the Windows and FortiGate add-ons read. \- \`tx\` and \`txf\` return an empty or whitespace-only line as its own text. \- Template records piped to \`| sendalert tenx_dml_to_kv\` are each read from their \`\_raw\`, so every template is stored under its own hash. \- The field map tool and its saved searches are no longer part of the app. Where a field map is installed, move its source off the map before upgrading, as the README's Upgrading section describes. \- Requires the Log10x Receiver at release 1.1.181 or later and Splunk Enterprise 9.4 through 10.6. After upgrading the app, restart Splunk.


Short Description:
Send Splunk the logs that sampling and filters keep out to fit the license, on that same license. Compact events take a fraction of the volume and expand back byte-identical at search time; classic dashboards keep their SPL, and one command covers the search bar, saved searches, alerts and the REST API.


Description:
With the Log10x App, Splunk can index compact log events and still search, chart and alert on the original lines. The 10x Receiver stores each event as a template hash plus the values that change, so a stream of repeated patterns takes less of the license. On the OpenTelemetry demo, Splunk's license meter counted 63.91% fewer bytes, encoded events and templates included, and every line expanded back byte-identical with the Receiver settings in the installation steps (measurement: https://github.com/log-10x/benchmarks/tree/main/splunk-license). The same license then holds more: sources that were sampled, filtered or kept out of Splunk to stay under the limit can come back, or the license can be smaller. To search by what the lines say, write the tx macro in front of an ordinary search: index=my_index `tx` "payment failed" NOT retry. It runs as native SPL in the search bar, Dashboard Studio, saved searches and alerts, and NOT, OR, groups, phrases, field conditions, and values such as IP addresses and hostnames behave as they do on the original data. Classic dashboards keep their SPL: the browser sends each panel's search to the app, which rewrites it on the server. An alert created in the app's Compile Alert view is compiled once into a native saved search. The 10x Receiver produces compact events, and it is free on up to 10 nodes (https://www.log10x.com/pricing). No sign-up is required: with no license token it runs the full product on up to 10 nodes, air-gapped, with no expiry (https://doc.log10x.com/manage/license/). The app itself is open source under the MIT license.

item.title: MCP Watch - v1.2.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
MCP-Watch 1.2.0 Detection overhaul. MCP traffic is now identified from the provenance stamp the Splunk MCP Server writes to \_audit (provenance\="MCP:\:\"), so the official server works out of the box with no lookup editing. NEW \- Provenance-based detection: every MCP query is tagged with its server and tool, whatever account it runs under. \- Real time windows: the time range is read from the audit event (apiStartTime/apiEndTime), so ranges the MCP server passes as API parameters are scored correctly. \- Query cost: result count, events scanned and run time per query, plus a "Most expensive queries" panel. \- MCP server telemetry on the Activity dashboard: tool latency, rejected logins by source IP, SPL refused by the server's safety check. \- Alert: Unlisted MCP Account (MCP queries from an account not in mcp_users.csv). \- Alert: MCP Authentication Failures (5 or more rejected logins per source IP within 15 minutes). \- Access matrix shows actual tool use, including tools that the deny policy forbids but an account called anyway. CHANGED \- Six dashboards consolidated into four: Overview, Activity, Risk, Access. Bookmarks to the remaining views keep working. \- Alerts are per-result with per-user suppression and non-overlapping 5-minute windows. \- The four reports are no longer scheduled. Nothing read their results; re-enable scheduling locally if you e-mail them. \- Objects are no longer exported globally (export \= system removed). FIXED \- Wide-time, wildcard-index (index\="\*", index IN (\*), index\=\_\*) and export/delete detections that missed MCP traffic. \- The "more than 100k results" risk bonus never fired. \- Liveness status was global instead of per MCP server. \- Distributed deployments: REST calls pinned to the local search head; indexer-side remote\_\* audit copies excluded so queries are not counted twice. (not yet verified on a cluster) \- Index scope now includes inherited indexes; telemetry fields are no longer double-counted. UPGRADE NOTES \- If your own searches append earliest\= or user\= directly after the mcp_audit_searches macro, move the time range to the dispatch settings and filter with "| search user\=...". \- The "no time bound" flag now has weight 3, so expect "Risky queries %" to change. Also includes the 1.1.x releases: multi-signal detection (user agent + endpoint), liveness heartbeats, a unified Access & Tools view, and dashboard correctness fixes. AppInspect (precert, cloud tags): 0 failures. Self-test: 80/80 fixtures pass. Full changelog: [https://github.com/ALPERKESKE/mcp-watch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ALPERKESKE/mcp-watch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)


Short Description:
Tracks AI agent activity in Splunk by analyzing _audit and _internal logs to surface MCP server queries, flag anti-patterns, and report REST endpoint usage.


Description:
MCP-Watch provides visibility and governance for AI agents operating against Splunk through the Model Context Protocol. The app surfaces every SPL query executed by MCP servers, flags anti-patterns such as wildcard index searches and overly wide time ranges, and reports on REST endpoint usage. It reads exclusively from Splunk's built-in _audit and _internal indexes, requiring no additional data ingestion or dependencies. Administrators configure a lookup table with the Splunk usernames their MCP servers authenticate as, and the app then tracks query volume, identifies quality issues, and enables per-user tool access governance. Four dashboards present MCP activity across operational and compliance dimensions, while scheduled searches and alerts provide ongoing monitoring of agent behavior.

Rate limits are respected with back-off. - Status dashboard: collections per data type, records written, minutes behind, errors, how late data arrives. - Python standard library only, no third-party packages. Short Description:
Two animated clock visualizations for Splunk Dashboard Studio: a smooth **analog** clock face (with optional digital readout) and a seven-segment **digital** LCD clock. Timezone-aware, themable colours, optional phosphor glow. No data required — drop one on any dashboard for a live, always-current clock.


Description:
Dashboard Studio has no built-in clock, yet operations walls, NOC status boards, world-clock panels and "as of now" headers all want a live, ticking time display. **Realtime Clock** adds two purpose-built custom visualizations that render the current time entirely client-side at 60fps — no streaming data, no scheduled searches, no backend. **Analog Clock** — a smooth analog face with sweeping hands, tick marks, an optional digital readout and day/date line, and a configurable phosphor glow. Hand, second-hand and tick colours are all configurable. **Digital Clock** — a seven-segment LCD-style display with a blinking colon, 12/24-hour modes, optional seconds, a date line, ghost (unlit) segments for an authentic LCD look, and a phosphor glow. Both support **local time, UTC, or any IANA timezone** (e.g. `Europe/London`, `America/New_York`, `Asia/Tokyo`), so a single dashboard can show a row of world clocks. Because the time is computed in the browser, the clocks stay accurate to the second regardless of search refresh intervals. Built as standard `studio_visualization` custom viz, themable to light/dark, and dependency-free.

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Release notes: https://github.com/livehybrid/TA-uk-open-data/releases/tag/v1.0.6


Short Description:
Modular inputs for open UK datasets, with a configuration UI. Ingests UK Carbon Intensity (api.carbonintensity.org.uk — half-hourly national intensity + generation mix) and NHS England monthly A&E attendance statistics. No API key. Idempotent, checkpoint-based, safe to run on any interval.


Description:
**UK Open Data** is a UCC-framework built add-on that brings two well-known open UK datasets into Splunk with no API key and no external dependencies beyond outbound HTTPS. **Carbon Intensity** — polls the National Grid ESO Carbon Intensity API (`api.carbonintensity.org.uk`) and indexes, per half-hourly settlement period, the national forecast/actual gCO₂/kWh and intensity band (`carbonintensity:national`) plus the generation mix by fuel type (`carbonintensity:generation`). Ideal for carbon-aware scheduling, ESG dashboards and "greenest time to run" decisions. **NHS A&E (monthly)** — scans the NHS England "A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions" pages, downloads each monthly CSV you haven't already loaded, and indexes one event per provider plus a national TOTAL row (`nhs:ae:monthly`) — type 1/2/other attendances, 4-hour performance and over-4hr counts. Great for healthcare performance and public-sector analytics. Both inputs are **idempotent**: they checkpoint what they've already indexed, so they're safe to run on any interval without creating duplicates. Carbon re-emits only un-settled recent periods until their actual value lands; NHS only loads months it hasn't seen. Built with the Splunk UCC framework — full configuration UI, per-input index/interval settings, and standard logging.

Adds search-time field extractions for Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) and ASA syslog message IDs that neither the Splunk Add-on for Cisco ASA nor the Cisco Security Cloud app extracts. Install it alongside either add-on: it only adds fields, and leaves their parsing, event types, tags and CIM mappings as they are. - Failover and high availability: unit switching to active/standby, interface monitoring, link status, VPN and WebVPN HA status and progression. - VPN: IKEv1 and IKEv2 tunnel events, IPsec terminations, AnyConnect client messages and large packets, WebVPN sessions, UAUTH entries, SAML relay-state failures, VPN filter ACL hits. - NAT and traffic: PAT pool exhausted, translation and xlate failures, fragment limits and drops, GRE and IP-in-IP connections, reverse-path-check and protocol denies, IPv6-ICMP denies, DNS drops. - Inspection: SIP, DCERPC. - System and chassis: FTD Linux and FXOS chassis syslog (process, sudo commands, chassis sign-ins, commands and session ends), configuration backups, interface line protocol, routes added/deleted, telemetry, ASP queue full, trustpoint export failures. - Every regex accepts both %FTD- and %ASA- prefixes and is anchored on its own message ID, so it runs only on that message. - Unique class names (EXTRACT-ftdx_*), so nothing in other add-ons is replaced. - Field names follow the Splunk Add-on for Cisco ASA (src_ip, dest_ip, src_port, dest_port, src_interface, dest_interface, transport, user, vendor_action, reason), so its normalization and CIM mapping pick them up. - Search-time only: no inputs, no index-time settings, no scripts. Description:
Sandfly is an agentless intrusion detection and incident response platform for Linux. Sandfly automatically analyzes Linux hosts for intruders 24 hours a day without loading any software on your endpoints. Additionally, Sandfly can retrieve hardware, operating system and related data for analysis in Splunk. Sandfly works across virtually all Linux distributions immediately without risk to stability or performance. The Sandfly Security Add-on for Splunk is a technology add-on that ingests events from a Sandfly Security server using the Sandfly Security REST API. This add-on (TA-sandfly-security) ingests data into your specified index and sets the correct sourcetype for each event. Events are ingested as JSON formatted events. Review the Details tab for a list of all supported sourcetypes. The Sandfly Agentless Security for Linux App includes dashboards, reports and logic for analyzing data ingested from a Sandfly server such as security alerts, suspicious activity and general software and hardware metrics. Data retrieved by Sandfly can also be used by Splunk users to build anomaly detection models, incident response and insights into software and hardware versions of your Linux fleet.

item.title: Vyrux Security - v1.2.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Vyrux Security 1.2.0. Everything since 1.1.0. **Hosts** - Hosts sending, silent and new for every log and index, Find a host, and host issues and alerts when hosts stop sending. **Alerts and issues** - Silent-log, host and root cause alerts follow each issue's state. A snoozed or suppressed issue sends no alert; when a snooze ends the issue opens again and alerts if the problem is still there. - A suppressed over-firing rule comes back when its alerts a day double. - An alert reaches each channel once; a channel that was down gets it when it is back. **Trust and access** - Every record is shown only to people whose Splunk roles can search the indexes it is about, including run history, collector health and approvals. - Every write goes through the Vyrux service and is checked for the person before it is saved. A stale page cannot undo a colleague's change. - Approvals cover the exact content asked for and what it replaces, for rules, parsers and suppressions. - Parser plans cannot set Splunk's own fields (host, index, source, sourcetype, _time). **Rule checks** - A search Splunk stops at its time limit is an error, never a count of zero. - The intent check reads names with fewer false readings and proves each mismatch with the rule's own events. - Macro arguments are filled in the same way everywhere, so no index is hidden in a macro. **Background scan** - One failing stage no longer stops the scan. Upgrades from earlier builds are applied once per build, and any failure is shown on System health. Full notes: the Release notes page in the Vyrux guide.


Short Description:
Know your Splunk security monitoring works. Vyrux checks that your logs arrive, your detection rules can fire and your ATT&CK coverage is real.


Description:
Your SOC depends on three things every day: the logs arrive, the logs parse, and the detection rules can fire. When one of them breaks, Splunk does not tell you. You find out after an incident, when the alert you expected never came. Vyrux checks all three every 15 minutes, inside your own Splunk. When a log stops arriving, Vyrux opens an issue, names the detection rules that can no longer fire, and alerts your team in Microsoft Teams, Slack or email. When a rule cannot fire, Vyrux says why: a missing field, macro, lookup or data model, a search window shorter than the log's delay, or scheduled runs that never finish. It also says who owns the fix. When many rules break for one reason, such as a firewall upgrade that changes the log format, Vyrux shows the one cause and the one fix that restores them all. Your MITRE ATT&CK coverage is measured from rules that actually work, not from rules that merely exist. Vyrux then helps your engineers fix what it finds, with Parsing Studio, a rule intent check, a Tuning Lab and Chuka, an optional AI detection engineer. Nothing changes in Splunk until a person deploys it, and you can require a second person to approve each change first. Vyrux is a Splunk app, not a SaaS service. It runs on your search head, respects every person's Splunk permissions, and keeps your logs in your Splunk.

Monitoring OpenShift brings your OpenShift clusters into Splunk: for the platform team that runs them, the application teams that deploy to them, and the security team that audits them. When a release goes wrong on OpenShift, the evidence is spread out: container logs on every node, the journal, events the API server keeps for about three hours, the audit logs of four API and OAuth servers, and the control plane's Prometheus endpoints. On a cluster many teams share, each team also needs its own data and its own alerts, and the platform team needs rules that hold for every project. Description:
Attack Path Intelligence shows how an attacker could reach your organization's most critical assets, and whether your detections would catch them. The app models attack paths as Crown Jewel → Attack Surface → Attack Vector. Each path gets a priority score based on the crown jewel's criticality, the jewel-surface relationship, the vector's relevance, the surface's exposure and the evidence level. The evidence level says whether a vector was observed in logs, confirmed by a vulnerability scanner or only inferred from the architecture. Every vector is mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and the app matches those techniques against your detections. You can use Splunk Enterprise Security correlation searches, read through their MITRE annotations, or a detection inventory lookup for rules outside ES. The result is a coverage view per vector, per path and per crown jewel. It also gives you a ranked detection engineering backlog and a list of disabled detections that would increase coverage if enabled. Optional live panels use the CIM Network_Traffic and Web data models to show real activity against the assets of each attack surface. Everything is lookup-driven and configurable: scores, weights, risk thresholds, MITRE match weights, data sources and CIM fields. The app ships with sample content for a fictional organization, so you can explore the dashboards before modeling your own environment.

Requires the Splunk Common Information Model (CIM) add-on. \## New dashboards \*\*Compliance\*\* \- \*\*CJIS Policy Area Scorecard:\*\* posture and findings rolled up to the 13 CJIS Security Policy areas (5.1 to 5.13), with a click-through to each area's controls. \- \*\*Gaps and Actions:\*\* controls that are not implemented, with owner, due date and days overdue, plus controls whose review is overdue. \- \*\*Incident Log:\*\* an append-only record of reportable incidents and whether and when each was reported to the state CJIS Systems Agency (CJIS 5.3, NIST IR-6). \- \*\*Evidence Pack:\*\* one page for an auditor: posture summary, every control with status and findings, audit retention against your requirement, weekly snapshots and status history. Export to PDF or CSV. \- \*\*Setup and Data Readiness\*\* (first item in the menu): shows, for each CIM data model, whether it is accelerated and has data, which controls have the data they need, which scope lists are still empty, and which indexes are searched. \*\*Monitoring\*\* \- \*\*Encryption in Transit (SC-8 / SC-13):\*\* allowed connections over protocols that do not encrypt traffic, with a "what to fix" recommendation for each, and weak TLS versions when certificate data is present. \- \*\*Network Boundary (SC-7):\*\* allowed versus blocked traffic, reachable services, top blocked sources and ports, and firewall changes. \- \*\*Remote Access (AC-17):\*\* remote logons, most active remote users, failed logons by source, and users signing in from more than one country. \- \*\*Vulnerability and Patch Status (SI-2 / RA-5):\*\* open critical and high vulnerabilities, how long they have been open, and failed or pending updates. \*\*Investigation\*\* \- \*\*Finding Triage (IR-4 / IR-5):\*\* acknowledge, assign, close or mark a finding a false positive, with a note and a full history of who changed what and when. \- \*\*Source / IP Investigation:\*\* logons, firewall traffic, intrusion signatures and findings for a single address. \## Improvements \*\*Trustworthy defaults\*\* \- Every control now ships as \*\*not assessed\*\*. Nothing is pre-marked as implemented. \- Control status changes are recorded with who and when. The posture editor requires an owner and accepts an optional due date. \- A weekly \*\*Evidence Snapshot\*\* search records each control's status and findings over time (off by default). \*\*Findings\*\* \- Each condition is now \*\*one finding\*\* (for example, one source failing logons) that is updated on each run, with first seen and last seen times. Previously a persistent condition added a new finding every hour. \- Triage decisions are stored separately, so re-running a search never undoes them. \- Findings are kept for a configurable number of days (default 365). \*\*Detections\*\* \- \*\*Brute force then success:\*\* now checks that the success came after the failures. It replaces the separate Cross-System Correlation search, which duplicated it. \- \*\*Privileged group membership (AC-6):\*\* now works with classic Windows event logs, which it previously missed, and covers more groups plus removals. \- \*\*File integrity (SI-7):\*\* limited to watched locations (system files, startup and autorun keys, services) and ignores known noise, so it no longer floods. It stays off until you supply Sysmon data and change windows. \- \*\*Log source silent (AU-5):\*\* per-source limits, and silent hosts on the CJIS device list. \- \*\*Malicious code (SI-3):\*\* uses the CIM Malware data model instead of one vendor's data. \- \*\*MFA (IA-2):\*\* uses the CIM Authentication data model. \- \*\*Configuration changes (CM-3):\*\* reports changes outside approved change windows. \- \*\*New: cleartext protocols (SC-8):\*\* creates findings for high-risk unencrypted protocols such as FTP, Telnet, POP3, IMAP and LDAP without TLS. \- \*\*Account exclusions:\*\* machine and Windows system accounts are ignored by default, and you can add your own service accounts in \`cjis_account_exclusions_local.csv\`. \- The after-hours window, brute-force threshold and silent-source limit are now settings you can change. \*\*Dashboards and documentation\*\* \- Dashboards no longer show machine-account and logoff noise in the account-change and privileged-logon tables. \- Menu names now include their control numbers. \- New in-app documentation: Getting Started, Using Finding Triage, Using the Incident Log, Scorecard / Gaps and Actions / Evidence Pack, Monitoring and Investigation Pages, and a Settings Reference. \## Upgrading from 1.0.x \- \*\*Findings:\*\* findings written by earlier versions used a different key. After upgrading, old findings remain until they age out and can appear next to new ones. If you want a clean start, you can clear them by running \`| inputlookup cjis_findings | where 1\=0 | outputlookup cjis_findings\`. This deletes all findings. \- \*\*Control status:\*\* your existing status records are kept. Only new installs start as "not assessed". \- \*\*Lookup files:\*\* Splunk keeps existing lookup files when an app is upgraded, so new rows in shipped CSVs do not appear on upgrade. Replace the file if you want them. \- \*\*New settings (macros):\*\* \`cjis_findings_retention_days\`, \`cjis_required_retention_days\`, \`cjis_review_interval_days\`, \`cjis_bf_threshold\`, \`cjis_silent_default_minutes\`, \`cjis_after_hours_start\`, \`cjis_after_hours_end\`, \`cjis_fim_scope\`, \`cjis_fim_noise\`, \`cjis_remote_access_filter\` and \`cjis_exclude_accounts\`. Defaults are in the Settings Reference. \## Requirements \- Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud Platform 9.x or 10.x, on a search head. \- The Splunk Common Information Model (CIM) add-on with the data models you use (Authentication, Change, Intrusion_Detection, Network_Traffic, and optionally Malware, Vulnerabilities, Updates and Certificates). Accelerate the models for speed. The Setup and Data Readiness page tells you which are missing. \## Known limitations \- The finding triage and incident log pages write to the KV store, so Splunk shows a one-time "risky commands" warning. Review the search and choose Run Query Anyway. \- A closed finding stays closed if the same condition happens again. Check its last seen time and reopen it if needed. \- SI-7 needs Sysmon file and registry events and real rows in \`change_windows.csv\`. \- Status is a self-assessment by your team. The app records and reports it but cannot prove a control is implemented. \- Multi-agency scoping is not included in this release. \- Protocol detection in Encryption in Transit is by port number, so services on non-standard ports are not classified.

item.title: Cloudflare Audit Logs Addon for Splunk - v1.1.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Please provide a read-only API token for the Cloudflare account whose audit logs Splunk will collect. Grant Account / Account Settings / Read, and limit the account resource to the specific account. Supply its Account ID and send the token through our approved secret-sharing channel. If client-IP filtering is enabled, allow the actual outbound IPs of our Splunk collector. No write permission or Global API Key is requested." WHY THIS PERMISSION This TA calls GET /client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/audit_logs. The endpoint lists Account Settings Read or Account Settings Write as accepted permissions. Choose Read for least privilege; Write is not necessary for this integration. Source: Cloudflare's account audit log API reference: [https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/audit_logs/methods/list/](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/audit_logs/methods/list/) Do not substitute Access: Audit Logs Read. That permission covers Cloudflare Access authentication logs, not the account audit endpoint used here. Zone / Logs / Read and Logpush permissions are not required for this TA's request. Permission definitions: [https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/reference/permissions/](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/reference/permissions/) TOKEN SETUP 1\. An authorized Cloudflare user opens My Profile > API Tokens > Create Token and creates a custom token. Token creation does not give that user access to accounts or privileges they did not already have. 2\. Set policy type Account, permission Account Settings, access Read. 3\. Limit Account Resources to the account(s) authorized for collection. Prefer a dedicated token scoped to the single account for each input. 4\. Choose an expiry/rotation policy. If IP filtering is used, allow the actual collector egress IPs. The Splunk Web hostname's DNS address is not evidence of its outbound/NAT IP. Obtain Cloud egress information from your Splunk administrator or support team. 5\. Store the displayed secret securely. Enter it directly in the TA's Bearer Token field. Do not include "Bearer ", quotes or surrounding whitespace. 6\. Use the 32-character Account ID, not a Zone ID or account display name. Cloudflare also offers account-owned tokens. Use them only after confirming support for this endpoint and your organization's token-creation policy. Neither a Cloudflare password nor a Global API Key is accepted by this TA. Instructions and resource scoping: [https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/create-token/](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/create-token/) VALIDATE THE ACTUAL ACCESS Saving the Splunk form validates its format and securely stores the token; it is not proof that Cloudflare authorized retrieval. Enable one input and check for "Cloudflare poll completed" in the internal logs. HTTP 200 with success\=true and result\=\[] means no records were returned. HTTP 401/403 means the credential/access checks above still need review. Token validity alone does not prove permission to the requested account. This release uses the v1 account endpoint, not the separate v2 /logs/audit, organization audit-log or Zero Trust Access authentication-log APIs.


Description:
Cloudflare Audit Logs TA for Splunk is designed to integrate with your Cloudflare Cloud audit logs with the Splunk platform. This add-on focuses on data monitoring, enabling you to bring Cloudflare activities into Splunk in real-time.

CIM field profile: for every data model and source the app samples events and measures each CIM field - how often it is filled, how often it only holds placeholders such as unknown or -, and whether its values follow the CIM definition (expected values, number type, port, IP, hash and MAC shapes). Field definitions are read from the data models installed on your search head, so custom models and newer CIM versions are covered automatically. Parsing and time: unparsed and partially parsed sources, multi-line and future-dated events, indexing latency and likely time zone offsets. Recommendations for unmapped sources suggest the data model, tags, key CIM fields and the add-on to use. No setup is needed: after install, first-run searches build the analysis automatically within minutes and scheduled searches refresh it every 4 hours. Defaults are light (7 days, acceleration summaries only, 200-300 sampled events per source); every window, sample size and limit is a macro, and the Overview shows the p90 run time of each job with tuning recommendations. Short Description:

Description:
TrackMe Broker lets TrackMe on Splunk Cloud reach the systems on your own network: remote Splunk instances (Heavy Forwarders, Deployment Servers), self-managed Cribl Leaders and webhook receivers. From a Splunk Cloud stack those destinations cannot be reached, because the stack cannot connect into your network. TrackMe Broker reverses the direction. This add-on runs on a Heavy Forwarder on your side, asks the stack for work over its REST API on port 8089, makes the HTTPS call locally and posts the answer back. Every connection starts on your side: you open nothing inbound. - Deny by default: the forwarder reaches only the targets you declare on it, whatever the stack asks for. - Encrypted end to end: each request and response is sealed for one paired forwarder (AES-256-GCM, keys on P-256), on top of HTTPS. - Paired, not trusted blindly: you accept each forwarder in TrackMe after checking its key fingerprint. - Highly available: run two forwarders in one broker; they share the work, and one carries on if the other stops. - Least privilege, FIPS-approved cryptography: the add-on authenticates with an account holding only the trackme_broker role. Requires TrackMe 2.4.24 or later on the stack. Documentation: https://docs.trackme-solutions.com/product_guide/integ_broker.html

Description:
The Credential Hunter app scans raw data in existing Splunk indexes to identify credentials that were indexed by accident, including cleartext passwords, API keys, tokens, and private keys. It employs a two-stage detection approach that combines term-index prefiltering in Splunk with regex verification in Python to minimize performance impact while maintaining accuracy. The app supports both full historical scans and continuous monitoring modes, with a configurable pattern catalog that allows administrators to enable or disable specific credential types based on their environment. Findings are stored in KV store collections and presented through dedicated dashboards for investigation, false positive management, and pattern tuning. The scanner operates as a scripted input that runs continuously but performs actual scans at administrator-defined intervals of 30 or 60 minutes. Configuration is managed through a Control room dashboard where scan intervals, event slack hours for late-arriving data, and retention policies can be adjusted without editing configuration files.
